_comment: GENERATED FROM legibility.json -- do not hand-edit; regenerate instead. The same frames with every VFX node disabled, so the question 'does the POSE alone read as an action' can be answered rather than argued. That question is the one a critic settled by saying "legibility and correctness are inversely correlated -- the effects you can't miss are the ones that read as objects; the one that reads as a genuine action is carried by the pose." This file had drifted once: three weapon pairs were added to legibility.json and not mirrored here, so the pose test silently covered 7 pairs while the judged set had 10.

shots._note: Charge held past the 1067 ms threshold. This was the weakest frame in the set and the only low-confidence call a critic made: charging runs inside the Idle state, so the pose WAS the idle pose and the only differences were the blade's colour and a soft ground glow — 'if the glow had been absent I would have called it IDLE with confidence 5 and been wrong'. There are now two hard-edged cues: a held anticipation pose (the `charge` clip, which is why expect_clip is no longer `idle`) and an outlined teal ground ring that closes inward. capture_offset waits 8 frames so the ring has finished converging — the charge is a HELD state, so any frame of it is representative, and the first frame of a 110 ms convergence is the least so.

shots._note: REGRESSION COVER for a rendering fault, not just another action frame. A spin on the river bank, where the expanding ground ring grows out over the water. A critic reported 'three or four thin black concentric arcs on the water surface with nothing inside them ... nobody would think spin attack; they would think the water is broken', and it was this: the ring is OPAQUE so it writes depth, the water is blend_mix so it erases the ring's fill without writing depth, and the outline pass — which reads the pre-transparent depth buffer — contoured a shape that was no longer visible. Diagnosed by freezing the frame and hiding one node at a time; with the ring hidden every arc vanished. actors/player/water_line.gd holds the fix and the full write-up. This pair exists so the fault cannot come back unnoticed: pair6 happens to be waterside too, but one position is a coincidence, two is coverage. The bank here sits BELOW the river surface, which is exactly the case a constant height offset cannot handle.
shots.name: pair7_action

shots._note: CONTROL for the AXE pair, and the first shot holding anything other than the sword. The loadout is advanced by the F4 `cycle_item` action, which is the only way a shot list can change what the character is holding: tools/capture.gd reaches the game through InputMap and nothing else. The cycle is SEQUENTIAL and persists across shots, so the order of the shots below is load-bearing — one press per pair, in the idle frame, which is also why the action frame of each pair needs none. Loadout.cycle() records the item as found WITHOUT the found banner, or a 30-point line of text would sit across the bottom of every frame here.
shots.name: pair8_idle

shots._note: The axe mid-swing, on the SAME clip the sword uses (slash_a) at 0.625x playback. Nothing about this frame is axe-specific code: the wind-up is 183 ms instead of 133 and the live window 167 instead of 100 because items/axe.tres asks for a slower rate. What a critic should be able to see is a top-heavy wedge rather than a straight blade, and a longer, deeper ribbon.
shots.name: pair8_action

shots.name: pair9_idle

shots._note: THE HIGHEST-RISK FRAME IN THE SET, and the reason the set was extended. A drawn bow is a HELD POSE WITH NO MOTION, structurally identical to the charge frame a critic called the weakest here: 'only the blade's colour changed — if the glow had been absent I would have called it IDLE with confidence 5 and been wrong'. So the draw is carried by three things and none of them is a tint: both arms leaving the silhouette in OPPOSITE directions with the chest turned side-on, an opaque black-outlined arrow nocked on the string, and — at full draw only — the same hard-edged ground ring the sword's charge uses. capture_offset 44 puts the frame past the 500 ms draw and past the ring's 110 ms convergence, so this is a FULL draw; a partial one would be a weaker read by design and is the frame to add next if this one passes.
shots.name: pair9_action

shots._note: Shield up. Also a held pose with no motion, and the same risk as the bow draw. The slab is raised ABOVE AND OUTSIDE THE RIGHT SHOULDER rather than held in front of the chest, which is deliberate: CLAUDE.md records that the only screen space an over-the-shoulder camera does not already own is above the head and outside the shoulders, and a 0.68 x 0.88 m board held in front of a 1.34 m torso is a board the camera looks THROUGH the character to see. With one equip slot this frame also has to answer 'what am I holding', because nothing else does.
shots.name: pair10_action
